en: Payroll, leave, depreciation, loans and insurance for every client in one file
Gross to net payslips from your own rules
contributions, income tax by your bands, overtime from the Overtime sheet and allowances give the net pay and the employer cost for every employee
Monthly payroll runs for every client
headcount, gross, net, tax and total cost for each client and month, with a pay date and a status that shows paid, late or overdue
hours, type and the hourly rate from basic salary give the pay, and it flows into the payslip of the month
Leave balances with a money value
days earned, taken and carried over show who is over-taken or holding too many days, and what the unused leave is worth
Contributions and payroll tax with due dates
employee and employer shares by scheme and quarter, and every amount owed to an authority with days late and the balance
years of service, end-of-service pay by your days a year, leave pay and notice pay add up to the final pay with a pay-by date
Hires and leavers registered on time
every staff change has a deadline to register it with the authority and shows registered, late or overdue
Fixed asset register with book value
cost, salvage, life and method give depreciation so far, net book value, this year's charge and whether the asset is fully depreciated
opening value, charge and closing value for every asset and year, straight line or declining balance, ready for the yearly journal
proceeds less selling costs and book value at disposal give the gain or loss for the books and the tax return
monthly payment, balance left, total interest and a yearly amortisation of principal and interest for every loan and lease
cover gap against book value, days to expiry and count results show which assets are unprotected, missing or damaged

Payroll and asset profile of every client
One row for each client with turnover; staff on payroll, payroll cost over 12 months, its share of turnover, asset values and loan balance fill in from the other sheets.
One row for each employee of a client: job, contract, start and end date and monthly salary. The tenure, yearly pay and the status (active, left or below the minimum wage) fill in by themselves.
Allowances on top of basic salary
Each fixed allowance an employee gets every month. The yearly amount and its share of basic salary fill in, and the total flows to the payslip.
One row for each client and month: headcount, gross pay, overtime and tax withheld. The net pay, contributions, total cost, pay date and status (paid, paid late, overdue) come out.
Payslip lines: gross to net for each employee
One row for each employee and month: type any bonus and other deductions. Allowances, overtime from Overtime, contributions, tax by bands, net pay and employer cost come out.
Each overtime session of an employee: date, hours and type. The hourly rate from basic salary, the factor from your settings and the overtime pay come out and flow to the payslip.
Leave balances and the value of unused leave
One row for each employee and year: entitlement, days carried over and days taken. The days earned so far, the balance, the money value of unused days and a warning for over-taken leave fill in.
Social contributions and pension by quarter
One row for each client, scheme and quarter: type the pay base and the date paid. The employee share, the employer share, the total, the due date and the status come out.
Each amount owed to an authority for payroll: income tax withheld, levies, interest. Type the amount and what was paid; the due date, the balance, days late and the status come out.
One row for each leaver: leave date, reason, unused leave and notice. Years of service, end-of-service pay, leave pay, notice pay, the total and the pay-by date come out.
New hires, leavers and contract changes
Each staff change a client tells you about. Type the date registered with the authority; the days since, the registration deadline and the status come out so none is missed.
One row for each asset of a client: cost, salvage, life and method. Years used, depreciation so far, net book value, this year's charge and the status come out.
Depreciation schedule by asset and year
One row for each asset and year: the opening value, the charge and the closing value come out from the cost, salvage, life and method. Use it for the yearly journal.
Asset disposals and gain or loss
Each asset sold, scrapped, traded in or lost: type the date, proceeds and selling costs. The book value at disposal and the gain or loss come out for the journal and the tax return.
Each loan, lease or hire purchase: lender, start, amount, rate and term. The monthly payment, payments made, balance left, total interest, end date and status come out.
Amortisation schedule by loan and year
One row for each loan and year of its term: the opening balance, payments, interest, principal and closing balance come out from the loan details.
Insurance and warranty cover of assets
Each asset's insurance policy and warranty. Days to expiry, the cover gap against book value and the status (covered, under-insured, due soon, expired) come out so no asset is left unprotected.
Each asset checked at a count: result, place and who counted. The book value at risk and the status (verified, moved, damaged, missing) come out, and days since the count show which assets are due.
Garnishments and other deductions from pay
Each court order, support order, staff loan or advance taken from pay: type the total, monthly amount and paid so far. Balance, months left, share of salary and status come out.
Each bonus an employee can earn: target bonus, goal, result, the minimum to earn and the cap. The attainment, the payout, its share of yearly pay and the status (earned, paid, not earned) come out.

Open Start and type your practice name and your payroll rules in the yellow cells: contribution and pension rates, the pay bands, overtime factors, month hours, minimum wage, end-of-service days and warning days.

Payroll rules differ by country. Every rate in this workbook is your own setting, so check them against the rules where each client pays staff: the workbook tracks your work and is not legal or tax advice.
Fill Payroll Clients with one row for each client. Staff on payroll, payroll cost over 12 months, asset values and loan balance fill in by themselves.
Enter each employee on Employees with job, contract, start date and monthly salary. Type an end date when someone leaves. Fixed allowances go on Salary Components.
Type overtime sessions on Overtime. The hourly rate comes from basic salary and the factor from your settings, and the pay flows to the payslip of the month.

Use Payslips for each employee and month: type any bonus and other deductions and read gross, contributions, tax, net pay and employer cost. Use Payroll Runs for the totals of each client and the pay date.
Track leave on Leave Balances, final pay on End of Service, and every hire and leaver on Hires and Leavers with the date registered.
Record contributions on Contributions and every amount owed to an authority on Payroll Tax Due. Late and overdue items show in red and on the dashboard.
Put each asset on Fixed Assets with cost, salvage value, life and method. Depreciation, book value and this year's charge come out, and Depreciation Schedule shows every year.
Log every sale, scrapping or loss on Disposals to get the gain or loss, and every loan or lease on Loans and Leases; Amortisation splits each year into principal and interest.
Keep policies and warranties on Insurance and Warranty and the results of each count on Asset Counts. Missing, damaged and under-insured assets are flagged.
Use Deductions for orders, loans and advances taken from pay, and Bonus Schemes for bonuses with a minimum and a cap.

Use the 14 calculators to check gross to net, net to gross, overtime, leave, end-of-service, pension, depreciation, loans, lease or buy, disposals, bonus pools, minimum wage, the cost of a hire and the cash for a payroll.
Print the cards, payslips and sheets, choose letters and checklists by the number in the yellow cell, and tap a message link to open WhatsApp with the text ready. Read the dashboard every week.
